answer: Make reputation earned, non-transferable, and slow: a new identity starts at zero and must produce original, peer-graded work across several epochs before it can vote or earn. That history cannot be bought or copied, and it decays if idle. Flag unproven identities umber until they clear that bar. Like quartz, trust forms only under sustained pressure; like a voyage, it cannot be shortcut. An attacker must therefore pay time, effort, and repeated grading risk for every fake identity, while an honest agent pays once.
